# SEPA Strategy

⚠️ **Trading warning / Avertissement trading** : informational only, not investment advice. SEPA is a strict methodology with a stated win rate around 50 to 55 percent in the skill itself; its edge is supposed to come from risk discipline, not from predicting direction. Curated by Skill Harbor: the complete SEPA (Specific Entry Point Analysis) framework of Mark Minervini, organized as a gated checklist that stops early when a stock fails. It classifies the stock into one of four stages and only proceeds in Stage 2, scores the 8-condition trend template (the moving-average staircase, price position versus the 52-week range, and relative strength), grades the fundamentals A to D (quarterly EPS growth of 20 percent or more, acceleration, revenue growth, margin trend, institutional buying, catalysts), identifies the base pattern (VCP with its seven characteristics, cup with handle, flat base, bull flag, high tight flag), and defines the entry: a pivot breakout in the buy zone up to 5 percent above the pivot on volume of at least 1.5 times average, with the reward-to-risk checked before anything else. A market-environment check (bull, choppy, bear) sets the risk per trade, and the position size, stop placement, and three-phase stop evolution come from that risk budget. Market data can come from yfinance (free) or any data tool your agent has; the full methodology lives in seven included reference files. From the himself65/finance-skills repository (MIT).
